item: Row 255: the WAL soak decides which checkpoint attempts are evidence by the scan's own sequence and a commit after the snapshot opened, never by comparing two threads' clocks
summary: Release note: no change you can see; a test that failed on macOS runners now judges what it means to. Cause measured: a reader that opens when every frame of the log is already copied takes SQLite's read-mark slot 0, which TRUNCATE does not wait for, so with no frame committed after the snapshot a TRUNCATE answers busy=0 under it (on an emptied log and on a full one a PASSIVE copied); on a runner whose writer had not committed yet the never-releasing mutants were counted as cleared. Reproduced with a held writer: the old clock window judged the mutant green, the new evidence rule finds no evidence and calls the round inconclusive.
